problemStatement.formal: Enumerate the 13 Archimedean vertex types, verify their positive angle defect, prove they are distinct, and record their Euler data.
problemStatement.plain: Back the Archimedean-solids classification entry with checked combinatorial data: the 13 listed vertex types all pass the angle-defect test, are distinct, and include Euler-count records.
whyMatters: Archimedean solids are the semi-regular analogue of the Platonic solids.
Angle-defect and Euler-data checks give a concrete verified combinatorial core for the classification story.
The Lean file carefully separates checked finite data from the full geometric classification theorem.

proven: The file defines face-size lists for the 13 Archimedean vertex types (Lean: archimedeanTypes).
Each listed vertex type is verified to have positive angle defect, and the combined list check is proved (Lean: all_archimedean_valid).
Combinatorial vertex, edge, and face data are recorded in ArchimedeanData values satisfying Euler's formula.
The list has length 13 and contains no duplicate vertex types (Lean: archimedean_count, archimedean_distinct).
The file verifies example facts including the snub dodecahedron defect data and truncated icosahedron soccer-ball data (Lean: snubDodecahedron_tight, soccerBall_is_archimedean, soccerBall_data).
open: The final geometric completeness statement is represented only as a placeholder theorem over True; this entry should not claim a full formal classification proof beyond the checked finite data.
knownResults.goal: Document the verified finite Archimedean-solid data while keeping the full geometric classification caveat explicit.
